description: The bar chart visually compares the average performance of five distinct training methods—labeled on the horizontal axis as 'Standard,' 'Self-RAG,' 'FactTune,' 'ClInGS (w/),' and 'ClInGS'—across 11 datasets, with performance values plotted on the vertical axis labeled 'Average Performance,' which spans from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The bars, each uniquely colored (orange for 'Standard,' olive for 'Self-RAG,' lime green for 'FactTune,' steel blue for 'ClInGS (w/),' and royal blue for 'ClInGS'), are arranged in ascending order of height from left to right, reflecting increasing performance. The 'ClInGS' method, represented by the tallest royal blue bar, achieves the highest average performance at approximately 60, while 'FactTune,' shown in lime green, exhibits the lowest performance at around 52. The 'Standard' and 'Self-RAG' methods, depicted in orange and olive respectively, show similar performance levels near 54, with 'Self-RAG' slightly lower than 'Standard.' The 'ClInGS (w/)' variant, in steel blue, falls between 'FactTune' and 'ClInGS' at approximately 55. The chart visually emphasizes the consistent superiority of the 'ClInGS' method over all others, particularly over its variant 'ClInGS (w/),' and highlights the relative stability of 'Standard' compared to the modest decline in 'Self-RAG.'
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average performance across five training methods on 11 datasets. The horizontal axis lists the methods: 'Standard,' 'Self-RAG,' 'FactTune,' 'ClInGS (w/),' and 'ClInGS,' in ascending order of performance. The vertical axis represents 'Average Performance,' ranging from 0 to 60, with intervals of 10 units. The 'ClInGS' method consistently outperformed all others, achieving an average performance of approximately 62, while 'FactTune' showed the lowest performance at around 48. The 'Self-RAG' method demonstrated a slight decline compared to 'Standard,' which maintained stable performance across datasets. The chart highlights the superiority of the 'ClInGS' methods, particularly the standalone 'ClInGS' approach, which exhibited a significant improvement over its variant 'ClInGS (w/).'
